result.issue: What can Harbor customers do today with export scheduling, what are its current limits, and what improvements are planned?

questions.text: What can Harbor customers do today with export scheduling, what are its current limits, and what improvements are planned?

answers.text:
Harbor workspace administrators can schedule a recurring CSV export of completed orders from the reporting page. The scheduler is available to all paid workspaces as of the September release. Each schedule sends a download link to the administrator who created it; the link expires after seven days. Scheduling does not grant access to other reports, and the recipient still needs an active workspace account to download the file.
A workspace may maintain up to five active export schedules. A schedule runs at most once per day, using the workspace time zone. The current CSV contains completed orders only; pending and cancelled orders are excluded.
The reporting group has approved work to add weekly and monthly cadence choices and to include cancelled orders as an optional export filter. Both items are planned for the next reporting cycle; neither has shipped. The group has also recorded a request for an API to create schedules, but no decision or target date exists for that request.

evidence.heading: Operational limits
evidence.content:

The delivery service retries a failed send twice over the following hour. A workspace administrator can check the most recent delivery result in the reporting page, but individual download events are not currently shown there.

evidence.heading: First measurement period
evidence.content:
Quartz measured onboarding time for customers who completed onboarding in the first period. The average was 20 calendar days from signed agreement to completed setup. The cohort contained 40 completed onboardings.

The measurement records elapsed calendar time, including weekends, rather than staff hours. Customers who had not completed onboarding by the end of the period were not included in this completed cohort.

The measurement records elapsed calendar time, including weekends, rather than staff hours. Customers who had not completed onboarding by the end of the period were not included in this completed cohort.

evidence.heading: Second measurement period
evidence.content:
For customers who completed onboarding in the second period, Quartz recorded an average of 15 calendar days from signed agreement to completed setup. This cohort contained 50 completed onboardings.

The operations team used the same start and end events as in the first period and included weekends. This is a descriptive comparison of completed cohorts, not a controlled experiment.

evidence.heading: Measurement context
evidence.content:
The onboarding dashboard reports elapsed time for completed setups. It does not count the number of hours employees actively worked on a setup. A lower average means completed customers moved from agreement to setup in fewer calendar days on average.

The dashboard does not establish why the average changed between periods; the customer mix and operating conditions may differ.
